herrera-esteli--habano.description: The first blend Willy Herrera made as Drew Estate's master blender, the original Herrera Estelí was renamed Habano in 2018; it wraps a Honduran binder and Nicaraguan filler in an Ecuadorian Habano leaf. Balanced and easygoing, it opens on white pepper and cedar, turns sweeter with coffee, cocoa and dried fruit, and suits morning or evening alike.

thirds.notes: White pepper and cedar lead, with a nutty undertone, a hint of baking spice and a toasty aroma.
The pepper recedes; coffee, cocoa and dried fruit come forward with a gentle sweetness and oaky wood.
Darker and richer, with cocoa and a chocolate-like aroma as some spice and strength return.

herrera-esteli--brazilian-maduro.description: Introduced in 2018 as the fourth Herrera Estelí blend, the Brazilian Maduro is made at La Gran Fábrica Drew Estate in Estelí with a plantation-grown Brazilian Mata Fina wrapper, a Connecticut River Valley Broadleaf binder and Nicaraguan filler. Willy Herrera's blend smokes earthy and slightly floral, with coffee, cedar and red pepper that grow as it burns.

thirds.notes: Slightly sweet, creamy coffee leads, with red pepper, cedar and wood in the background.
The coffee dries out as earth and wood step forward and the pepper and cedar grow.
Red and black pepper with cedar move to the front, over steady coffee and earth.

herrera-esteli--norteno.description: Herrera Estelí Norteño, from Drew Estate's Gran Fábrica in Nicaragua and rebranded in 2018, wraps a Mexican San Andrés maduro leaf around a spicy Honduran binder and long-aged filler from Estelí and Jalapa. Medium in strength, it begins with leather and baking spice, turns earthier with oak, and finishes smooth with a honeyed sweetness.

thirds.notes: Firm leather and baking spice, with black pepper early that softens into cinnamon-like warmth.
Earthier now, with oak taking the place of most of the leather, balanced by spice.
Earthy tones carry on as a honey sweetness builds, smooth and never bitter.
